curated-gf-gravitas-one-gf-noto-sans-heb: Gravitas One spreads its swollen letters wide, curves tapering to hairline wire. Noto Sans Hebrew sits beside it with open, wide-mouthed curves and a plain sans tallness, so the two feel like a shout answered by a relaxed murmur.
curated-gf-grechen-fuemen-gf-inconsolata: A faint wedge of pen pressure shows in every curve of Grechen Fuemen, friendly and loose (say, for a punk gig flyer). Inconsolata then lines up its fixed-width, code-style characters, and that handwritten-against-monospace tension is the pair's real hook.
curated-gf-grenze-gotisch-gf-victor-mono: Bold, dark and tightly packed, Grenze Gotisch lays a thick stripe of lowercase across each line. Victor Mono spaces its monospace glyphs loosely, with bowls left open on one side, so a lengthy page would feel like cold air after a crowded room (an engineering blog, perhaps).
curated-gf-grey-qo-gf-gentium-plus: Grey Qo looks hand-drawn, its terminals pressing inward and its middle sitting low and sparse. And Gentium Plus, a refined text serif with a wide pitcher-mouth in each c, gives the light script something steady to lean on (a travel journal, say).
curated-gf-grey-qo-gf-lato: Grey Qo has a casual, hand-drawn feel, with terminals pressing inward to leave a slim wedge of white (a gratitude journal might use it). Lato's wide, barely curled s keeps a longer read smooth.
curated-gf-griffy-gf-mooli: Griffy crowds its expressive glyphs together like pressed tiles, with the ends of each c never turning inward. Mooli's open, round sans letters stay clear at small sizes, so a longer read goes down easily.
curated-gf-griffy-gf-podkova: Podkova reads bookish and traditional, its c opening broadly. Griffy is the showoff of the two, packing heavier verticals into tight display lines, while Podkova is better for quieter, brief copy (an election campaign flyer, for instance).
curated-gf-gurajada-mulish: Mulish draws every stroke at a single weight, with horseshoe-open apertures. Gurajada squeezes its oversized small letters so tightly that they feel thick and closed, and Mulish gives that density room to breathe.
curated-gf-gveret-levin-fs-pilcrow-round: Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters close, yet big counters and curves that refuse to close keep it warm. Gveret Levin's rope-thick, hand-drawn heading sits above it, and over many lines the plain sans stays friendly without fuss.
curated-gf-hachi-maru-pop-gf-gilda-displ: Stretched-out spacing gives Hachi Maru Pop a relaxed, inviting look. Gilda Display, a text serif with swollen darks beside near-invisible hairlines, adds a sharper, bookish edge that makes the soft heading look even more easygoing.
